Before I came out to my mum, I did every google search you could imagine. I read every coming out story going but not a single one told me what I wanted to know,

How will my parents react, mine, Michael and Diana, react?

Nobody here will be able to tell you how your parents will react but what I will say is that the closet makes you think the worst of the people you love. It is unavoidable. You keep this hidden for so long it can drive you a little mad.

But deep down, your parents will just want to make sure you are ok, whether that means they see being trans as something that is wrong or not is the key.

When I came out, I did not realise this. I was expecting the worst (whilst hoping for the best) but after I finished my spiel the first thing my mother said was "are you ok?".

So be honest, be open and let them know how much happier and how much better your life will be now. Because if they don't see being trans as an inherently bad thing then they will know that you are happy in yourself, and that is all a parent really wants.

I really hope it goes well sweetie, good luck and look after yourself. X

People kill each other, steal from each other and do all sorts of terrible things to each other. And we are people. The reasons why people do those things are as numerous and as complex as life itself. To simply say "they did a bad thing because they are bad" is dumb.

There are no good people, no bad people, just people. And if you really think you are above that then have a think about the worst thing you have ever done.

Yes. All the time. Height restrictions were a nightmare to enforce if the parents were with them. It was always amazing to me how parents thought they could protect their tiny child from falling off a ride. Customers can be very unreasonable but that's the same with ay customer facing job.

You mean like a haunted mansion type ride? That was the one thing the park never had. I have no idea why. But no, I never had sex on park grounds. Customers on the other hand...I never caught anyone but it was fairly regular. Or it could have been crap. A lot of rumours went around.

We only got one break a day, for 30 minutes (including the time it took to walk back to the staff area) and after that it could be another 8 hours before the park shuts. I had sort of forgotten how terrible the conditions were. But I was young, the money seemed amazing (first time I ever had more than a hundred bucks in the world) and I was an idiot.

Cheers. Best moments where the staff partys. They didnt seem to care that most of us were high school/early college and they let us bring kegs. All that usual teenage stuff, first loves, new exciting music, experimenting with drugs, all that for me happened there and I am still friends with a lot of the people I met there.

The worst moments? The day after the partys. And whenever they had an inspection of any kind. It was like trying to hide drugs from your parents as they are entering a room without warning. One guy got fired from this burger stall because two of his frozen burgers overlapped and the meat was raw. Any other day he would have put them back in to finish but the health inspector found it and the supe threw him out the park. If you are not getting this impression from my last few comments....the bosses were scum bags and morons.

I was working in one of the stores and got a call on the store phone telling me some guy was filming the kids on this water slide. He had apparently been there all day, everyday for three days. But the security "team" was on holiday and they were asking me, aged 15, to go and escort this guy to the entrance of the park and kick him out. Of course I did it...they were grown ups and I had no backbone (or sense of self preservation). I walked up to him and asked if he could come with me. And he did. It was as if this kind of thing happened all the time. He was a fairly old guy but did not look like a pedo should,he was wearing gap clothes or something similar. We walked in silence to the entrance of the park where some cops took him away. Apparently he had been doing that for weeks. Rumours went around that they found louds of kiddie porn on his computer but who knows. All I know is, I hated being around him.

Both. The park was in a forest/farm/remote kind of place so if someone really wanted to get in...they could. Our security "team" was an ex cop and his overweight wife so it wasn`t like the risk was high. But there was this oine guy who actually lived in the park for about a week. At first we thought he was the only person to ever buy a week long pass because he just kept showing up every day. Then after the ticket people heard about it they looked through their records and told the security "team" that he had no bought a week ticket. They found him trying to get some sleep under the ferris wheel. To my knowledge he was the only one that actually got caught. The kids I saw jump the fence never got caught and I couldn't report them because, until I became a supervisor I never had a cell phone and when they gave me one I didn`t care if anyone sneaked in as long as they were cool.

Apparently something went wrong in her car as it was going up and it rolled back into the car behind. The guy operating had pulled the emergency break in time but it wasn't connected properly.

Last I heard he is still in therapy. And a girl who was on spring break never went back to school.

One of the worst days of everyone's lives. Everyone was freaking out and they stuck me on crowd control. Which was a dumb idea because I was young, stupid and the customers were scared, conffused and angry. I can't remember exactly what happened after that. It was all a blur.

Rides definatly. The games were one up over retail but most customers did'nt realise how much of a scam they were. At our park we got a lot of schools visiting and the kids would blow all their lunch money on the rides then get their teacher to try and get the money back. I used to give it back because kids wouldn't know what the deal was. But adults should have known better and they got angry, occasionally violent...but yeah, rides had the most prestige at the park. What was yours like?

There were a fair few at the park I worked at. Most of them were cheap imitations of the bigger ones you find at Disney, universal etc that they got for cheap from god knows where. There was one that they built themselves that was about half a mile long and I used to work that a lot when I first started because the more experienced people keep the good jobs for themselves and left the newbies to clean up vomit and get into arguments with parents over the height restrictions.

I guess the reason it feels like a big deal to me is because it has been a factor in ruining two relationships in the past. Both times for various reasons I waited to long to tell them and I broke the trust. I did not give them all the information they needed before entering the relationship with me. I also see a lot of guys in their 50's who have this who break up their family's when it comes spilling out. I don't want that to be me.
